about: Helper words: every word used in definitions, examples, stories and quizzes that is not (yet) taught in a lesson. When a later lesson teaches one of these, move it into that lesson.

entries.en: this, that (ce, cet, cette); it (c'est = it is)
to go (ça va = it's going fine)
to make (+ adjective); to give back
the (le or la before a vowel sound)
if; whether; (answering a negative question) yes!
more; (ne … plus) no longer, not any more
badly; (avoir mal à) to hurt: j'ai mal aux dents = I have toothache
here you are; there it is
French; (le français) the French language; (un Français) a French person
Martin (a family name, or a man's first name)
Lyon, a big city in France
Montreal, a big French-speaking city in Canada
some (plural of un / une); also de + les
Marseille, a big city in the south of France
Canada (le Canada; au Canada = in Canada)
to do, to make (ça fait = that makes)
there; to it, about it (j'y vais = I'm going there; il y a = there is)
by; per (deux par deux = two at a time)
him; (to) him, (to) her (je lui parle = I talk to him/her)
France (la France; en France = in France)
of the, from the (de + le); some
on the floor, on the ground
flea market, garage sale (lit. “empty the attic”)
oneself, himself, herself (se laver = to wash)
serious (ce n'est pas grave = it doesn't matter)
Minou (a common name for a cat)
to want (je veux = I want; je voudrais = I'd like)
to the, at the (à + les); with (gâteau aux pommes = apple cake)
can, to be able to (je peux = I can)
to sting; to be spicy (ça pique = it's spicy)
you need, it takes, you must
it, him (object: je le prends = I'll take it)
it, her (object: je la prends = I'll take it)
them (object: je les prends = I'll take them)
him, her, it (le or la before a vowel: je l'aime = I love him/her)
some, any; of it, of them (j'en veux = I want some)
(to) them (object: je leur parle = I talk to them)
you, yourself (object: ça te va = it suits you)
high, tall; (le haut) the top; (en haut) upstairs, up there
trainer, sneaker (des baskets) — not le basket, the sport
less; minus; (time) to: deux heures moins dix = ten to two
must, to have to (je dois = I must)
middle (au milieu de = in the middle of)
until; as far as (jusqu'en avril = until April)
to get annoyed, to get worked up
to pass; to stop by (passer à la poste)
to meet (se rencontrer = to meet each other)
end, tip (au bout de = at the end of)
Saint-Jean (a cathedral and old district in Lyon)
Tête d'Or (a large park in Lyon)
since; for (+ time): depuis un an = for a year
edge (au bord de l'eau = by the water)
Victor Hugo (French writer, author of Les Misérables)
going back to school or work after the summer (in September)
national (la fête nationale = the national holiday)
just, right (juste après = right after); fair
shape, form; (en forme) fit, in good shape
to give (as a present), to offer
to present; to introduce (je vous présente… = let me introduce…)
Lille (a city in the north of France)
gratin (a baked dish with a golden, cheesy top)
(turns a sentence into a yes / no question) Est-ce que tu viens ? = Are you coming?
what? (Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? = What are you doing?)
has he…? does he have…? (il a, as a question)
has she…? does she have…? (elle a, as a question)
is he going…? (il va, as a question)
is she going…? (elle va, as a question)
is there…? are there…? (il y a, as a question)
Annecy (a town on a lake, in the Alps)
turn; trip, outing (faire un tour = to go for a walk or a ride); (la tour) tower
shade; shadow (à l'ombre = in the shade)
the Saône (a river that meets the Rhône in Lyon)
Mont Blanc, the highest mountain in the Alps (4,806 m)
Fourvière, a hill in Lyon with a famous basilica
la Croix-Rousse, a hill in Lyon (the old silk workers' district)
Provence (a region in the south-east of France)
bank (une carte bancaire = a bank card)
guard, ranger (un garde du parc = a park ranger)
to fill; to fill in (a form)
(il faut) it's necessary, you have to
(s'occuper de) to look after, to take care of
forum, fair (un forum des métiers = a careers fair)
to run, to manage, to lead
leave, time off (un jour de congé = a day off)
luck; chance, opportunity (bonne chance ! = good luck!)
Quebec (the French-speaking province of Canada, and its capital city)
the Rhône (a big river that flows through Lyon)
Mount Royal, the hill in the middle of Montréal
in common, shared (les transports en commun = public transport)
poutine (chips with cheese curds and gravy, from Quebec)
right; law (avoir le droit de = to be allowed to)
inhabitant (les habitants = the people who live there)
birth (la date de naissance = date of birth)
for tourists (un voyage touristique = a holiday trip)
(se moquer de) to make fun of
to be born (je suis né(e) = I was born)
to fly away, to blow away
long live…! hooray for…! (vive les vacances !)
terrace (en terrasse = outside, at a café)
the Loire (France's longest river, famous for its châteaux)
return, way back (au retour = on the way back)
from (… on), as early as (dès le premier jour = from the very first day)
there was, there were (il y a, in the imparfait)
that much (pas tant que ça = not that much)
room, hall (la salle de classe = the classroom)
the bac (the big exam at the end of the lycée)
language, way of speaking (le langage familier = informal speech)
fairy (un conte de fées = a fairy tale)
single (not married or in a couple)
meeting, encounter (une application de rencontre = a dating app)
no, not a single (je n'ai aucune idée = I have no idea)
matter, deal; (les affaires) things, belongings; business
Pinocchio (the wooden puppet whose nose grows when he lies)
kiss on the cheek (faire la bise = to greet with a kiss on each cheek)
to beat; to hit (se battre = to fight)
hair (on the body or on an animal), fur
throat (avoir mal à la gorge = to have a sore throat)
what (as the subject: qu'est-ce qui se passe ? = what's happening?)
certain, sure; (before a noun) some, a certain
miss (a polite way to address a young woman)
blow, knock, hit (un coup de main = a hand, some help)
Montmartre (a hill and old artists' district in Paris)
there is some, there are some (of it, of them)
go ahead! go on! (to several people or politely)
that's it! done! there we are!
to go up, to increase; to raise
either, neither (moi non plus = me neither)
from (à partir de maintenant = from now on)
trouble, effort; sorrow (ça vaut la peine = it's worth it)
equal (ça m'est égal = I don't mind)
pinch (une pincée de sel = a pinch of salt)
state, condition (en bon état = in good condition)
log (une bûche de Noël = a Yule log cake)
as much, as many (autant de… que = as much / as many… as)
about fifteen; (une quinzaine de jours) two weeks
(after a noun with ce) this: ce mois-ci = this month
to put back; to put on again
resolution (les bonnes résolutions = New Year's resolutions)
bottom; back (au fond = at the back; du fond du cœur = from the bottom of my heart)
Christmas Eve or New Year's Eve dinner
to kiss; to hug (s'embrasser = to kiss each other)
progress (faire des progrès = to make progress)
whole, entire (le monde entier = the whole world)
flying (une voiture volante = a flying car)
